problem: Suppose that a matrix $A$ has characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda )=(\lambda +2)(\lambda -5)^{19},$ the rank of $(A-5I)^{5}$ equals $12,$ and the rank of $(A-5I)^{6}$ equals $9.$ If a basis of ${R}^{20}$ consists of linearly independent generalized eigenvectors of $A$, how many of these are generalized eigenvectors of rank $6$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5?$

mathematical_assessment.explanation: Rechecking gives fifth-power nullity 20 − 12 = 8 and sixth-power nullity 20 − 9 = 11. The intended difference is 3 (option b), but these data are impossible: successive nullity increments are nonincreasing, so a sixth increment of 3 requires the first five increments each to be at least 3, forcing fifth-power nullity ≥ 15 rather than 8. The earlier uncertainty therefore remains; no such matrix exists.
